bill.title: A joint resolution disapproving the rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to "Overdraft Lending: Very Large Financial Institutions".
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-10.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects overdraft fee revenue and regulatory compliance obligations at very large financial institutions.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would nullify a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule that limits overdraft fees at very large banks. The rule, published in December 2024, requires these institutions to either cap overdraft charges at $5, set a higher justified amount, or treat overdrafts as credit subject to Truth in Lending Act disclosures. If enacted, the resolution would prevent the rule from taking effect, leaving existing overdraft fee practices in place.

bill.title: FIND Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly protects firearm manufacturers, dealers, and trade associations from discrimination in federal contracting.
Banks and financial institutions that provide services to federal contractors would be affected if they maintain policies restricting business with firearm entities.
Defense contractors frequently hold federal contracts and may need to review policies regarding firearm-related business relationships.
Insurance companies that contract with the federal government would need to ensure their underwriting policies do not discriminate against firearm businesses.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit federal agencies from awarding contracts to companies that discriminate against firearm manufacturers, dealers, or trade associations. Contractors would be required to certify they have no policies that discriminate against firearm-related businesses and will not adopt such policies during the contract term. The requirement would apply to both prime contractors and subcontractors, with penalties for violations, but would not apply to sole-source contracts.

plain.whoItTouches: People who own or buy guns.

bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Federal Communications Commission relating to "Addressing the Homework Gap Through the E-Rate Program".
bill.latestActionText: Held at the desk.

industries.rationale: The bill would eliminate a new revenue stream for wireless carriers and broadband providers who sell hotspots and mobile connectivity services to schools and libraries under the E-Rate program.
The bill would remove schools' and libraries' ability to purchase subsidized internet access equipment for students and patrons, affecting their budgets and service delivery.
The bill would affect manufacturers and vendors of Wi-Fi hotspot devices that would have been purchased through the expanded E-Rate program.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would overturn a Federal Communications Commission rule that allows schools and libraries to use E-Rate program funds to purchase Wi-Fi hotspots and mobile internet service for students and patrons to use at home. The FCC rule was designed to help students complete homework and access educational resources outside of school buildings. If this resolution passes, that rule would be nullified and schools and libraries would no longer be able to use E-Rate funds for off-campus internet access.

bill.title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
bill.latestActionText: Motion to proceed to consideration of measure made in Senate. (CR S4276)

industries.rationale: The bill directly authorizes procurement of defense equipment, military construction projects, and sets policy for defense contractors and aerospace manufacturers.
The bill authorizes specified military construction projects and extends authorization for projects from previous years.
The bill requires review of critical materials including boron carbide, copper foil, and synthetic diamond, and authorizes investments in critical minerals for defense applications.
The bill sets policy for cyber operations, cybersecurity, and artificial intelligence programs within the Department of Defense.
The bill authorizes Department of Energy national security programs and investments in critical minerals and materials that may affect energy sector supply chains.

bill.plainSummary: This bill authorizes funding and sets policy for Department of Defense programs, military construction, and Department of Energy national security activities for fiscal year 2027. It covers procurement of military equipment like aircraft and ships, sets personnel levels for active duty and reserve forces, establishes policies for military healthcare and compensation, and addresses cyber operations and artificial intelligence. The bill also authorizes investments in critical materials and minerals for defense manufacturing and approves specific construction projects at military installations.

plain.whoItTouches: People in the military, and their families.

bill.title: Fair Access to Banking Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates how banks and credit unions may deny financial services to customers.
Digital asset firms have frequently reported being denied banking services, making them likely beneficiaries of fair-access requirements.
Firearms businesses have reported service denials from banks citing reputational risk, which this bill would prohibit.
Cannabis and related businesses have faced banking access challenges that this bill's requirements could address.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restrict banks, credit unions, and payment card networks from refusing service to customers who comply with the law. Financial institutions could only deny service based on documented, quantitative risk standards set in advance, and could not cite reputational concerns as a reason. Violations would trigger penalties including loss of federal deposit insurance, exclusion from electronic payment systems, and potential civil lawsuits by affected customers.

bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Department of Energy relating to "Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Consumer Gas-fired Instantaneous Water Heaters".
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 12.

industries.rationale: Manufacturers of gas-fired instantaneous water heaters would be directly affected by the nullification of energy efficiency standards that govern their product design and compliance costs.
Natural gas suppliers have a stake in standards that affect the efficiency and market competitiveness of gas-fired appliances versus electric alternatives.
Energy efficiency standards for gas appliances can influence the relative market share of gas versus electric water heating systems.
Contractors and builders who install water heaters would face different product availability and compliance requirements depending on whether the standards remain in effect.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would overturn a Department of Energy rule issued in December 2024 that set new energy efficiency standards for gas-fired instantaneous water heaters (commonly called tankless water heaters). The DOE rule required these appliances to meet stricter energy conservation requirements. If this resolution passes, the new standards would be nullified and would not take effect.

bill.title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses organized theft targeting retail operations and e-commerce platforms.
The bill explicitly covers theft from interstate and foreign shipments, affecting logistics and shipping companies.
The bill addresses online marketplaces and social media platforms where stolen goods are sold, potentially creating new compliance obligations.
The bill expands money laundering statutes to cover prepaid cards and gift cards, affecting payment processors and card issuers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal authority to prosecute organized retail theft and supply-chain crime. It allows prosecutors to aggregate the value of stolen goods over a 12-month period to meet felony thresholds, makes these offenses predicate crimes for money laundering charges, and authorizes asset forfeiture. The bill also creates a temporary coordination center within the Department of Homeland Security to help federal agencies work together on these cases.

bill.title: Protecting Access for Hunters and Anglers Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects manufacturers and sellers of lead ammunition by limiting federal authority to regulate their products on public lands.
Manufacturers of fishing tackle containing lead would face fewer potential federal restrictions on their products' use.
Sporting goods retailers selling lead ammunition and tackle would benefit from reduced regulatory uncertainty around these product lines.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prevent three federal agencies—the Fish and Wildlife Service, Bureau of Land Management, and Forest Service—from banning or regulating the use of lead ammunition or fishing tackle on federal lands and waters. The agencies could still impose restrictions in specific locations if they determine, based on field data from that site, that lead use is the primary cause of a wildlife population decline and the state agrees to the regulation. Certain existing regulations would remain in place.

bill.title: A resolution recognizing community care as an essential tool for meeting the health care needs of the veterans of the United States.
bill.latestActionText: Resolution agreed to in Senate without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S8874; text: CR S8874)

industries.rationale: The resolution emphasizes community care, which directs veterans to private hospitals and physician groups when VA facilities cannot meet demand.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution is a non-binding statement recognizing that community care—health services provided by private providers outside the VA system—is an important way to meet veterans' health needs. It urges the Department of Veterans Affairs to fully implement the 2018 law that created the Veterans Community Care Program, ensuring veterans can access private providers when the VA cannot serve them in a timely manner. The resolution does not change law or create new programs; it expresses the Senate's support for existing community-care arrangements.

plain.whoItTouches: Veterans and their families.

bill.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-12.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new content moderation obligations and 48-hour removal requirements on social media platforms and user-generated content websites.
New criminal prohibitions and mandatory restitution provisions would generate litigation and enforcement work related to intimate image publication.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would make it a federal crime to publish intimate images or videos of someone online without their consent, including computer-generated deepfakes, when the publication is intended to cause harm or involves a minor. Social media platforms and similar websites would be required to remove such content within 48 hours after receiving a complaint from the person depicted. Violators would face criminal penalties including prison time, fines, and mandatory restitution to victims.

plain.whoItTouches: Children, and the adults responsible for them. Anyone who uses the internet.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-1.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

plain.whoItTouches: People applying to live here, and their families here. People applying to come here, and their families here.

bill.latestActionText: Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
subjects: Drug safety, medical device, and laboratory regulation

industries.rationale: The bill directly targets insulin pricing and market practices, affecting pharmaceutical manufacturers' revenues and regulatory obligations.
Insulin cost caps or coverage mandates would alter health insurers' benefit design and reimbursement structures.
Changes to insulin pricing and access may affect prescribing practices and patient cost-sharing at the point of care.

bill.plainSummary: The bill's title suggests it addresses insulin pricing or access, likely building on previous INSULIN Act proposals that capped out-of-pocket costs for insulin users. Without the full text or detailed summary, the specific mechanisms—whether it imposes price caps, regulates manufacturer rebates, expands coverage mandates, or includes antitrust provisions—cannot be confirmed. The subject terms indicate it may involve competition rules, administrative enforcement, and oversight of drug pricing.
